A focus on equity is critical in the New Zealand context. It means recognising and responding to the diverse circumstances and needs of all our learners.

You will lead the delivery of financial, commercial, procurement, property, fleet and sustainability activities for the Ministry. The role provides strategic insight and direction, leads day-to-day operations and supports evidence-based decision-making across a significant operating and capital environment.

The Chief Financial Officer will drive excellence, service improvement and efficiency across the portfolio. You operate confidently at executive level, manage challenge constructively and build collaboration across the organisation.

  • Extensive experience in senior finance leadership roles within large and complex organisations.
  • Strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, accounting, investment and performance reporting.
  • Deep knowledge and understanding of relevant legislation, Treasury guidance and government processes.
  • Experience providing high-quality financial commentary and recommendations to senior leaders and external stakeholders.

job.title: Director Communications and Media
job.description:
• Shape how we communicate on matters affecting tamariki and rangatahi 
  • Deliver clear, consistent and impactful communications in a complex environment 
  • Drive media engagement, issues management and ministerial support

About Oranga Tamariki 
Oranga Tamariki works to ensure tamariki in Aotearoa are supported to flourish within loving whānau and communities. Guided by the belief that every child can thrive when surrounded by the right people and a safe, nurturing environment, more than 4,500 kaimahi work across the country to improve outcomes for tamariki, rangatahi and whānau. 

The Communications and Media function plays a critical role in helping the organisation tell its story, respond to scrutiny, engage effectively with stakeholders, and connect strategy with frontline delivery. This is an opportunity to lead that function at a pivotal time. 
 

About the Role 
This is one of the most senior communications roles in the New Zealand public sector. You'll shape strategy, media and stakeholder engagement for an agency operating at the centre of national scrutiny. Reporting to the Chief of Staff, you'll lead a team of around 26 across communications, media, content and channels, and be closely involved in the organisation’s most sensitive issues, including ministerial and government-facing communications. This is a hands on, close to the action role.  

This is a role that balances long term strategy with day-to-day responsiveness. One week you might be shaping an organisational communications strategy, strengthening internal engagement, or helping leaders think differently about connecting with frontline kaimahi. The next, you could be responding to urgent media issues, preparing material for ministerial engagement, or navigating sensitive public interest matters. 

Key areas of focus include: 
  • Leading the organisation's communications and media strategy 
  • Providing trusted advice to senior leaders and the Chief Executive 
  • Supporting ministerial and government facing communications 
  • Strengthening internal communications and employee engagement 
  • Building capability, accountability and consistency across the communications function 
  • Continuing to evolve media, digital and stakeholder engagement approaches 
  • Ensuring communications activity supports organisational priorities and delivers measurable impact 
This is a highly visible role with significant influence across the organisation and regular engagement with ministers, government agencies, media and external stakeholders. 

 
About You 
You are an experienced communications leader who combines strategic judgment with genuine hands on credibility. You understand the realities of operating in a high-profile environment and can move comfortably between executive advisory work, media engagement, crisis communications and organisational leadership. 

What you’ll bring: 
  • Significant senior communications and media leadership experience 
  • Strong understanding of machinery of government and ministerial environments 
  • Experience working in organisations operating under public scrutiny or significant stakeholder interest 
  • A track record leading high-performing communications teams 
  • Expertise across strategic communications, media management and reputation management 
  • The ability to provide clear, pragmatic advice in complex situations 
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and executive presence 
  • Understanding of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and experience engaging with diverse communities across Aotearoa 
Most importantly, you're someone who can combine leadership with delivery. You'll be comfortable setting direction, making decisions, supporting your team, and stepping into the detail when required. 


Why This Role? 
Opportunities to lead communications at this level are rare. This role offers the chance to shape the voice, reputation and engagement approach of one of New Zealand's most important public sector organisations. You'll work alongside experienced leaders, influence issues of national significance, and lead a capable team with the mandate to make a genuine impact. 

This is a Wellington-based position. 

 
How to Apply 
INSIDE Recruitment is managing this appointment. To apply, please include a CV and cover letter outlining your experience. For a confidential discussion, please contact Jeremy McLeod (jeremy@inside.co.nz). Applications close 12pm, Friday 25th September. 

Please note: You must be eligible to work in Aotearoa and able to pass a Ministry of Justice criminal history check.

The New Zealand Law Society Te Kāhui Ture o Aotearoa plays a vital role in supporting the legal profession and promoting the rule of law. Through its advocacy and law reform work, the Law Society provides independent, expert input on legislation, policy development, access to justice and constitutional matters that impact New Zealanders and the legal system.  


About the Role 
Reporting to the General Manager Policy, Courts and Government, you'll lead the Law Society's law reform function, providing strategic and operational leadership across a broad portfolio of legislative, policy and regulatory issues. 

This is a unique opportunity for an experienced legal professional who combines exceptional analytical capability with strong people leadership and stakeholder management skills. You'll oversee the development of high-quality submissions and policy positions, working with specialist committees, senior practitioners, government agencies, the judiciary and other key stakeholders to ensure the Law Society presents a clear, authoritative voice on issues affecting the profession and the administration of justice.  

The role operates at the heart of significant legal and public policy developments. You'll be responsible for analysing legislation and discussion documents, identifying issues and implications, coordinating expert input and helping shape the Law Society's response on matters relating to the rule of law, access to justice, human rights, constitutional issues and legal practice.  

As a trusted senior advisor, you'll also provide guidance to organisational leaders, support external advocacy initiatives, contribute to stakeholder engagement and represent the organisation in high level forums when required.  


What You'll Bring 
You're a highly credible legal professional with the intellectual capability to quickly understand complex issues and the emotional intelligence to influence a diverse range of stakeholders. You thrive in fast-paced environments, enjoy working across a broad range of legal topics and are motivated by the opportunity to contribute to matters of national importance.

  • A strong legal background gained in private practice, government, regulatory, policy, law reform, or in-house legal environments 
  • Experience analysing legislation, public policy, regulatory frameworks, or law reform initiatives 
  • Outstanding written communication skills, including drafting submissions, legal analysis, briefings, or policy advice 
  • Demonstrated experience leading, mentoring, or influencing teams, committees, or professional stakeholders 
  • The ability to build consensus and navigate competing perspectives across diverse groups 
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills and confidence engaging with senior legal, government, judicial and professional audiences 
  • Sound judgement, political awareness and the ability to operate effectively in complex environments

This is a rare opportunity to lead a respected and influential law reform function that has a genuine impact on legislation, public policy and the legal profession in New Zealand. 

You'll work alongside highly regarded legal professionals and subject matter experts, engage with important national issues and contribute to discussions that shape the future of New Zealand's legal framework. The role offers significant autonomy, variety, intellectual challenge and the opportunity to develop meaningful relationships across the legal and public sectors.  

You'll join an organisation with a strong sense of purpose, a collaborative culture and a deep commitment to promoting the rule of law and improving access to justice for all New Zealanders.

job.title: Chief Information and Security Officer
job.description:
• Enterprise-wide technology infrastructure and security mandate
  • Large-scale, regulated and 24-hour operating environment
  • Direct influence with executive leadership and the Board

SkyCity Entertainment Group is appointing a Chief Information and Security Officer to lead the functions that protect, sustain and strengthen its enterprise technology infrastructure environment. 

The mandate spans cyber security, infrastructure and technology operations, site reliability, application support, data engineering and data governance across SkyCity’s gaming, hospitality, entertainment and corporate operations. 

Reporting to the Chief Customer and Digital Officer, the CISO will lead the Group’s security and enterprise technology infrastructure. Working alongside the Group Digital Officer, they will ensure SkyCity’s digital ambitions are supported by secure, reliable and efficient platforms and services. 

The opportunity is to bring greater integration and effectiveness across a broad enterprise function. This includes strengthening cyber and operational resilience, improving critical service performance, and supporting technology innovation with expedience. 

The CISO will provide clear assurance to executive leadership, the Board and the Audit and Risk Committee, and lead the organisation’s response to significant technology and security incidents. 

The brief calls for a grounded, assured leader who remains composed under pressure and acts decisively when required. Intellectually curious and externally connected, they will stay ahead of emerging technology infrastructure and security developments, continually looking for better ways to strengthen services, reduce risk and enable the business. They will build trust across technical and business teams, strengthen accountability and bring people with them through change. 

We are interested in established CIOs, CISOs and senior technology executives who bring: 
  • Leadership experience within a large-scale, complex and continuously operating technology environment. 
  • Depth in cyber security, enterprise risk and regulatory assurance. 
  • Substantial accountability for infrastructure, technology operations, service delivery and business-critical applications. 
  • Experience maintaining resilient 24-hour services and leading the response to major outages or cyber incidents. 
  • Strong commercial judgement across investment, vendors and operating models. 
  • Credibility with executives, Boards, regulators and senior business leaders. 
  • A record of building capable leadership teams and delivering sustained change in complex organisations. 
Experience in a regulated, multi-site, customer-facing organisation will be highly regarded. 

This is a rare opportunity to influence the technology infrastructure and security direction of one of New Zealand’s most distinctive organisations, and to lead a function central to its resilience, performance and future. 

All enquiries and applications will be treated in strict confidence.

job.title: Senior Risk Manager
job.description:
• Senior enterprise risk role with broad organisational visibility
  • Work with senior leaders on complex, business-critical risks
  • Auckland preferred, other New Zealand locations considered

This is a senior enterprise risk role for someone who wants their work to be close to real business decisions.

You’ll be joining a large, complex New Zealand organisation with an established approach to risk management already in place. The foundations are strong, the work is visible, and the opportunity is to bring fresh thinking, sound judgement and practical challenge to an environment that is ready for the next layer of maturity.

This is not a role for someone who wants to simply maintain a risk register. It will suit someone who enjoys working with senior people, asking good questions, making sense of ambiguity, and turning complex issues into clear, useful insight.


About the role
As Senior Manager Risk, you will work across the organisation to support effective enterprise risk management.

You will partner with senior leaders to help identify, assess, monitor and report key risks. You will contribute to senior management and governance-level reporting, support the ongoing improvement of risk frameworks and processes, and help leaders make better-informed decisions.

The role works across a broad range of risk areas. These may include commercial, operational, regulatory, supplier, technology, project, financial, reputational and resilience-related risks.

You will not personally own every risk across the organisation. Your role is to help ensure the right risks are visible, well understood, appropriately owned, actively managed and clearly reported.

This is an influential role in a matrix environment, where outcomes are delivered through others. Success will come through credibility, relationships, judgement and the ability to bring people with you.


What success looks like
After 12 months, you will be known as someone who has lifted the quality of risk conversations across the organisation.

You will have built trust with senior leaders, improved the clarity of risk reporting, and helped connect risks that may otherwise have sat in separate parts of the business.

You will have brought useful challenge to an established risk environment, without trying to change things for the sake of it.

You will have helped make enterprise risk more practical, more visible and more useful to decision-making.

That is the heart of this role: making sure risk is not just reported, but understood.


What you’ll be doing
  • Providing practical enterprise risk advice to senior leaders
  • Supporting senior management and governance-level risk reporting
  • Helping identify, assess and monitor key and emerging risks
  • Supporting the use of risk appetite and tolerance in decision-making
  • Maintaining and improving risk frameworks, policies and processes
  • Working across multiple business functions to build a joined-up view of risk
  • Helping lift risk capability through guidance, facilitation and coaching
  • Bringing constructive challenge and fresh thinking to an established risk environment

About you
You will be an experienced enterprise risk professional who can operate credibly with senior stakeholders while staying practical and grounded.

You may currently be in a role such as Senior Risk Manager, Enterprise Risk Manager, Risk Governance Manager, Principal Risk Advisor, Risk and Compliance Manager, Head of Risk and Assurance, or a comparable senior risk role.

You will bring:
  • Strong experience in enterprise risk, risk governance or risk and compliance
  • Experience working in a large, complex or highly governed organisation
  • A practical understanding of enterprise risk frameworks
  • Experience contributing to senior management, executive or governance-level reporting
  • Exposure to risk appetite, risk tolerance, key risk and emerging risk processes
  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills
  • The ability to simplify complex issues and communicate clearly
  • Sound judgement, curiosity and commercial awareness
  • Confidence to challenge constructively
  • A continuous improvement mindset
Experience from large corporate, infrastructure, utilities, telecommunications, financial services, insurance, banking, government, Crown entity, listed company or other complex environments would be relevant.

The right person will be thoughtful, credible and commercially aware. You will be comfortable working with ambiguity, confident enough to challenge, and pragmatic enough to bring people with you.

This role will suit someone who wants enterprise risk to be useful, visible and connected to real business decisions.


Location
Auckland is preferred, although candidates from other New Zealand locations may be considered where there is strong alignment to the role.


How to apply
Please apply online with your CV.

Suitable candidates will be contacted and provided with further information about the organisation, role and process.

job.title: Legal and Commercial Advisor
job.description:
• Direct exposure to high impact investment decisions
  • Blend of legal, commercial and governance work 
  • Visible role in a newly established Crown Entity 

Join Invest New Zealand at an exciting moment in our journey. We’re a recently established Autonomous Crown Entity with a high-performance, collaborative culture — and we’re looking for a curious, practical legal professional who enjoys working at the intersection of investment, governance, and great process.


About us
Our purpose is to increase the flow of foreign direct investment into sectors with high growth and productivity potential — supporting long-term economic prosperity. We work on investments typically in the $100m to $1b range and help deliver the investment component of the Active Investor Plus (AIP) Visa scheme.


The opportunity
As our Legal & Commercial Advisor, you’ll play a key role in how we assess and support acceptable investments under the AIP visa programme. You’ll lead the investment product assessment work and support the AIP decision makers — making sure they have clear, timely information and that decisions and records are managed in line with relevant legal and regulatory requirements.


What you’ll be doing
  • Be the go-to person for queries about AIP investment criteria and process, working closely with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Pre-assess managed fund and direct investment applications and prepare clear summaries and recommendations for decision makers.
  • Maintain accurate records, including processes/procedures and material correspondence with applicants.
  • Own key risk management processes for the programme, including re-certification and the risk log.
  • Support relationships with key stakeholders such as Government agencies, fund managers and licensed immigration advisers.
  • Assist the General Counsel with Official Information Act requests from time to time.
 
What you’ll bring
  • An admitted lawyer (commerce and/or finance qualifications are an advantage).
  • 4–6 years’ PQE, including at least 2 years in private practice.
  • Strong commercial judgement and a sound understanding of the managed funds environment (or the motivation to learn quickly, supported by commercial/financial services experience).
  • Confidence working with governance and reporting requirements; board secretariat or legal executive experience is a bonus.
  • Understanding of New Zealand’s financial services regulatory environment.
  • A detail-focused mindset with the ability to assess and appropriately challenge information.
  • Clear, professional communication skills and the ability to build trusted relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.
  • A naturally curious, collaborative style—you enjoy being part of a small team and pitching in where needed.

Why join us?
You’ll be joining a small, ambitious organisation where your work will be visible and valued. We’re building strong foundations and practical ways of working—so you’ll have genuine scope to improve process, influence how we operate, and work alongside experienced colleagues who care about doing great work (and doing it well together).
